preview.instructions:
You judge how completely a product is understood — you do NOT decide whether it
is complete enough. That decision is made elsewhere from your scores.

Score each dimension from 0 to 1:
- purpose: what this is and why it exists
- users: who it serves and what they need
- core-behaviour: what the system actually does
- data: what it stores and what shape that takes
- constraints: technical, business, regulatory, operational limits
- edge-cases: failure modes and boundaries
- acceptance: how anyone…
preview.input:
# Understanding to assess
## Product
one-liner: A tool that extracts what you know about a product and identifies what is missing
purpose: To help users consolidate their understanding of a product and surface gaps in their thinking
users: Product managers, Teams exploring new ideas

## Open gaps
- [gap-1] purpose/Input method BLOCKING
- [gap-2] core-behaviour/Gap detection logic BLOCKING
- [gap-3] core-behaviour/Output presentation
- [gap-4] data/Knowledge structure BLOCKING
- [gap-5] acceptanc…

coverage.rationale: Core purpose is clearly stated—extract and consolidate product understanding and identify gaps—but the blocking gap on input method (gap-1) means we don't fully understand how users will provide the knowledge to extract.

User types are identified (product managers, teams exploring ideas) and their general need (consolidate understanding, identify gaps) is stated, but specific workflows and requirements remain unclear without knowing input/output mechanisms.

High-level behavior is stated but severely constrained by two blocking gaps: how input is received (gap-1) and how the system actually detects gaps (gap-2), plus a non-blocking gap on output presentation (gap-3) means the core mechanics are not understood.

No information on what data is stored, what structure represents product knowledge, or how that structure evolves; blocking gap-4 on knowledge structure prevents understanding the data model entirely.
No documented constraints regarding technical limits, business rules, operational requirements, or regulatory obligations.
No documented failure modes or boundary conditions; unclear how the system handles incomplete user input, incorrect gap identification, or users' metacognitive blind spots about their own knowledge.
Blocking gap-5 on success criteria means there is no documented way to verify the tool consolidates understanding correctly or identifies the right gaps.
No information on required integrations or external systems the tool must communicate with or depend on.

value.summary: The product has a clear high-level purpose and known user types, but understanding is critically limited by three blocking gaps: input method (gap-1), gap detection logic (gap-2), and knowledge structure (gap-4) that prevent the system from being specified. Two additional gaps (output presentation gap-3 and acceptance criteria gap-5) also constrain specification. Constraints, edge cases, data model, and integration requirements are entirely absent.
